tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative, scenario-driven phrasing ('Use this skill when...') and lists numerous explicit trigger contexts (model degradation, truncated responses, nondeterministic outputs, failed evaluation jobs, judge score swings, model comparisons, fine-tuned model shipping). It focuses on user-facing symptoms and intents rather than internal implementation, though it is somewhat long for a 'concise' description — however given the domain's complexity and the number of distinct triggers it needs to cover, this length is justified and still reads as a coherent set of trigger conditions rather than implementation detail.
tests.evidence: Diagnose and review model output quality and evaluation jobs on Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker. Use this skill when answers got worse or a model may hallucinate more, responses are cut off or end on max_tokens...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific: it defines check-ids, routing rules, read-only guardrails, finish-reason mechanics specific to Bedrock/SageMaker eval. It doesn't explain generic concepts like what an evaluation job is in general terms; it assumes the agent knows AWS basics and jumps to specifics.
tests.evidence: 'A shift from end_turn (natural completion) toward max_tokens (truncation) means outputs are being cut off — because prompts grew and crowded the output budget...' is domain-specific, not a generic explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed tables (check catalog, collection calls, metric thresholds) are kept in references/ and only summarized or pointed to in the body; the body itself contains short tables (Scope Model, Severity Definitions, Router table) that are navigational rather than exhaustive reference data.
tests.evidence: 'Every assessment is grounded in the check catalog checks-evaluation.md (load it before assigning any check-id or severity).' shows detailed catalog content is deferred to references/.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ (api-quirks.md, checks-evaluation.md, collection-reference.md, finish-reason-analysis.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md, router.md) has at least one markdown link in the body.
tests.evidence: '[checks-evaluation.md](references/checks-evaluation.md)' and similar links for all seven reference files appear throughout the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with explicit loading conditions throughout the body.
tests.evidence: 'load before any log query or metric read' for metrics-and-logs.md and 'load when a truncation or finish-reason shift is in question' for finish-reason-analysis.md.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.
tests.evidence: '[router.md](references/router.md)' and all other links follow this relative pattern.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-stakes operations (read-only guardrails, finding format, delegation payload columns) are highly prescriptive, while advisory sections (routing, synthesis, posture review) allow judgment and explain reasoning behind rules.
tests.evidence: 'Never call a mutating API — in particular CreateEvaluationJob, StopEvaluationJob...' is prescriptive for a fragile/safety-critical rule, while 'Assess only what the question or incident touches' leaves room for judgment.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where paths/tools diverge (Bedrock vs SageMaker, which service ran the job), the skill gives a clear decision rule rather than presenting equal options, and defaults to reading the caller's current region.
tests.evidence: 'Default to the caller's current region and say so.' and the service-check decision rule using DescribeTrainingJob vs GetEvaluationJob show a clear default/branch rather than a menu.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigation procedure (steps 1-5, routing table, check catalog usage) that applies across many different evaluation incidents, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: 'Work the steps in order... Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support' generalizes across any evaluation question.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has extensive gotchas-like content, explicitly structured in a 'Common wrong answers' section plus guardrails addressing non-obvious pitfalls like region-gating and no-datapoints traps.
tests.evidence: '"ListEvaluationJobs is empty, so no evaluation has ever run — CRITICAL." Bedrock evaluation is region-gated... confirm regional support first and report INFO/advisory' is a concrete pitfall correction.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: Output templates exist as assets (evaluation-report-template.md, sagemaker-evaluation-report-template.md) and the body defines the Findings block format inline, meeting the structured-output need.
tests.evidence: 'load [evaluation-report-template.md](assets/evaluation-report-template.md) for the Bedrock path and the posture review' shows templates are provided for structured output.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The only inline template is the short Findings block format, well under 20 lines; longer report templates are offloaded to assets/.
tests.evidence: The inline 'Findings\n<check-id> (<SEVERITY>) — ...' block is only 2 lines, far under the 20-line threshold.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three asset files (delegation-payload.json, evaluation-report-template.md, sagemaker-evaluation-report-template.md) are linked in the body.
tests.evidence: '[delegation-payload.json](assets/delegation-payload.json) is that prompt, finished (load when delegating evidence-gathering)' and similar links for both templates.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link specifies a clear condition for loading it.
tests.evidence: 'load when a report is requested on the Bedrock path or the posture review' and 'load when delegating evidence-gathering to a sub-agent' specify when to load.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset references use relative paths like assets/filename with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural Investigation Procedure section uses checkbox format with Step N naming, and the detailed subsections below it reference the same step numbers (Step 1, Step 2, etc.).
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support' followed by '### Step 1 — Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support' matching the checklist.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive dedicated self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output for errors (upgraded negatives, dropped rows, missing findings block) before presenting.
tests.evidence: '## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' with 'Scan the draft for an upgraded negative, sentence by sentence.' is explicit self-validation guidance.
